## Day 1 & 2 Quiz

Select an option, then click **Check** (or press **c**). Use **1**–**4** to pick an option, **q** to reset a question, **t** to shuffle question order.

Based on [Day 1 notes](day1.qmd) and [Day 2 notes](day2.qmd).

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Joe Cheng's opening quote, what is winning the battle between convenience and correctness?**

- Correctness
- [Convenience]{.correct}
- Neither — they're tied
- It depends on the model

## {.quiz-question}

**In Timothy Keyes's terminology, what is a "tool"?**

- [A function the LLM can ask the harness to run on its behalf]{.correct}
- A program that coordinates calls to an LLM
- An LLM using tools iteratively in a loop
- A prompt template stored in a skills folder

## {.quiz-question}

**In Keyes's patient-chart-summarizer evaluation, which harness pattern was both the highest quality *and* the cheapest?**

- Simple conversation
- Workflow (map-reduce over notes)
- [Agent (LLM chooses its own tool calls)]{.correct data-explanation="It only reads the notes it actually needs, instead of rereading everything like the workflow harness."}
- All three tied

## {.quiz-question}

**In the NYC Squirrel Count persona study, which persona preserved the most data with the fewest destructive changes?**

- [Data manager]{.correct}
- Data science student
- Environmental researcher
- They were all about the same

## {.quiz-question}

**What is the "lethal trifecta" cited in Neal Richardson's MCP talk?**

- Three pricing tiers for LLM APIs
- [Private data access + untrusted content exposure + ability to communicate out]{.correct data-explanation="Simon Willison's term — an agent combining all three can be tricked via prompt injection into exfiltrating private data."}
- Three categories of hallucination
- Three required fields in an MCP tool schema

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Winston Chang, why does total LLM conversation cost grow roughly *quadratically* with conversation length?**

- Output tokens get more expensive over time
- [Each request resends the entire prior conversation, so cost is a cumulative sum of growing requests]{.correct}
- Models charge a flat fee per conversation
- Caching becomes less effective the longer a conversation runs

## {.quiz-question}

**What is the single biggest cost lever Winston Chang highlighted?**

- Using only open-weights models
- [Prompt caching]{.correct data-explanation="Repeated input tokens served from cache cost roughly 1/10th the normal input-token price."}
- Turning off thinking/reasoning tokens
- Batching requests overnight

**What YAML-based tool did Hadley Wickham introduce for documenting a dataset?**

- data-diff
- [data-dict]{.correct}
- {commons}
- {ggdist}

**What does querychat deliberately restrict agent code execution to?**

- Any R or Python code

## {.quiz-question}

**In Christine Zhang's keynote, why does the NYT publish a uniformly shaded margin-of-error band instead of the more statistically accurate bell-curve band?**

- The bell curve is harder to compute
- [It's a compromise between statistical correctness and audience familiarity]{.correct}

**Why did the NYT withhold the election-night "needle" for the Michigan Senate Democratic primary?**

- A technical bug prevented it
- [Primary polling was unreliable enough that the needle would overstate confidence]{.correct data-explanation="The pre-election forecast was off by about 9 points, and a needle's dial swings feel more decisive than an equivalent line-chart movement."}
- Needles are never used for primaries as a matter of policy
- There wasn't enough reported vote data

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Sharon Wang's talk, what's the more durable question to ask instead of "what context do agents need?"**

- "What model should I use?"
- [What context do *you* need?]{.correct}
- "How much will this cost?"
- "Which harness is best?"

**Which of the following are things {commons} uses to route a question through trusted code rather than freehand generation?**

- Popularity of the language alone
- [A compelling reason — not switching by default]{.correct}
- Whichever language the client prefers
- Whatever the coding agent defaults to

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Wes McKinney's keynote, what three things become more valuable, not less, in agent-driven work?**

- Speed, scale, and automation
- [Judgment, taste, and agency]{.correct data-explanation="Without them, agent-driven work becomes slop that gets thrown away or left for someone else to maintain."}
- Memory, context, and tokens
- Architecture, testing, and documentation

## {.quiz-question}

**In McKinney's "Clanker Constitution," what does "act with judgment" mean?**

- Always ask permission before every change
- [Scale process/tooling to the size of the task — don't build a 5,000-line test framework for a minor feature]{.correct}
- Never make a decision without a human
- Maximize test coverage on every change

## {.quiz-question}

**Per McKinney (via Cory Doctorow), what is a "reverse centaur"?**

- A human assisted by a machine, like a bicycle for the mind
- [A machine assisted by a human, who just presses the buttons the machine can't press itself]{.correct}
- Two AI agents working without human oversight
- A human who refuses to use AI tools at all

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Charlotte Wickham, what accessibility standard does the ADA Title II web rule (and similar legislation) actually point to?**

- Section 508 only
- [WCAG 2.1 AA]{.correct}
- ISO 9001
- PDF/UA

## {.quiz-question}

**What was the single largest category of author-side accessibility violations Charlotte Wickham's tool found on quarto.org?**

- Color contrast failures
- [Missing alt text (98 violations)]{.correct data-explanation="Quarto will never generate alt text for you — only the author knows why a figure is there."}
- Missing skip-to-content links
- Broken heading order

## {.quiz-question}

**What is Quarto 2, per Emil Hvitfeldt and Carlos Scheidegger?**

- A minor patch release of Quarto 1
- [An entirely new, MIT-licensed codebase — a large chunk of Pandoc ported to Rust and compiled to WASM to run in the browser]{.correct}
- A rebrand of Quarto Pub
- A Python-only reimplementation of Quarto

## {.quiz-question}

**What underlying technology does Quarto Hub use to sync edits between collaborators?**

- A central SQL database with row locking
- [Automerge, an open-source CRDT for JSON data]{.correct}
- Git branches merged automatically every second
- WebSockets with a custom diff format

## {.quiz-question}

**In Leslie Emery's clinical data harmonization workflow, what are the three pieces of the system?**

- Raw data, a chatbot, and a spreadsheet
- [Data model files, harmonization config files, and pipeline code]{.correct}
- A vector database, an LLM, and a dashboard
- Trial data, a codebook, and a Shiny app

## {.quiz-question}

**In Mirian Lima's OSA Metrics workflow, what does the "save the story, not the answer" step actually export?**

- The full raw dataset used in the analysis
- [A `session.json` with the table schema, generating queries, and every query/chart pair — no raw data]{.correct}
- A PDF report with embedded charts
- A video recording of the analyst's screen

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Kelli Goggans, what's the first step when messy data doesn't fit the question?**

- Identify standards
- [Define your limits — decide what data you actually need and what's extraneous]{.correct}
- Refine your analyses
- Discard incompatible sources immediately

## {.quiz-question}

**In Yasha Kaushal's talk, what happened when the same merge prompt was run on the same 5 files in two different Claude Code sessions?**

- It produced an error both times
- [It silently produced different results — 407 households one time, 464 the next]{.correct data-explanation="Invisible failure, no decision trail, and a smarter model doesn't fix it — the fix is deterministic logic, not a better chatbot."}
- It took twice as long the second time
- It required a different prompt each time

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Max Kuhn, what is tidymodels' most effective way of building "wisdom" into an API?**

- Verbose prompt engineering
- [Guardrails baked into the API itself — e.g. naming the final-evaluation function `last_fit()` so you can't misuse the test set]{.correct}
- A chatbot that warns you after the fact
- Mandatory code review by a second analyst

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Sam Clark's "Three Agents" talk, what turned out to matter more than the underlying model?**

- The price per token
- [The harness — what determines whether a model's capabilities take the shape of real data science work]{.correct}
- The number of tools available
- The programming language used

## {.quiz-question}

**Besides "good to go," what other verdicts can Nicky Bell's Circuit tool return on an AI-generated analysis?**

- "Excellent" and "needs polish"
- [Provisional and walk away]{.correct data-explanation="Circuit is designed to say an analysis is unsolvable or fatally flawed rather than always producing an answer."}
- "A+" through "F"
- Pass and fail only

## {.quiz-question}

**What are Tyson Barrett's three buckets for any AI task?**

- Fast, medium, slow
- [Delegate, collaborate, own]{.correct}
- Easy, hard, impossible
- Trust, verify, reject

## {.quiz-question}

**Per Jenny Bryan's lightning talk, what makes a file name excellent?**

- It's as short as possible
- [It's machine readable, human readable, and sorts usefully]{.correct}
- It includes the author's initials
- It never includes numbers

## {.quiz-question}

**What problem does Thomas Lin Pedersen's Hephaestus rendering engine solve for ggplot2?**

- Slow rendering of large datasets
- [Exported plot images having the wrong aspect ratio/resolution/colors for a given presentation — solved via a dynamic, resizable `.hep` file format]{.correct}
- Lack of theming support
- Inability to export to PDF
